name: Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces
problem: Subquadratic alternatives to attention - linear attention, gated convolution, recurrent models, structured state space models - had not matched attention on language, and the paper diagnoses why: they cannot perform CONTENT-BASED reasoning, because their state transition and output are input-independent functions of the sequence.
mechanism: Selective state space models. Two changes to the SSM: (1) make the SSM parameters - the discretisation step size and the state matrix - FUNCTIONS OF THE INPUT, so the model selectively propagates or forgets information per token (this is the 'selectivity' and it is what enables content-based reasoning, but it also breaks the fast convolutional form); (2) to recover speed, design a hardware-aware parallel algorithm for the recurrent mode that scans the sequence in a memory-efficient layout. Mamba is then just these selective SSM blocks with no attention and no MLP.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claims (abstract): 5x higher inference throughput than Transformers, with linear scaling in sequence length; Mamba-3B outperforms same-size Transformers and matches Transformers twice its size on language modelling. The throughput claim's baseline class is 'Transformers' generally, not a named engine, so treat 5x as the paper's own generalisation rather than a reproducible decode-tok/s figure.

MERGED FIELD BY FIELD - nothing was silently dropped:
  mechanism: the retired record's text was materially fuller (1199 chars vs 570) and is RETAINED here rather than discarded. Its text: Makes the SSM parameters functions of the input, which is the whole contribution. The layer is a selective SSM: input x is projected to (delta, B, C) where delta_t = softplus(W_delta x_t + bias) is data-dependent, B_t and C_t are data-dependent, and the state updates h_t = exp(delta_t * A) h_{t-1} + delta_t * B_t x_t^T followed by y_t = C_t h_t + D x_t. Because B, C and delta now depend on the token, the model can selectively propagate or forget along sequence length per input, which is what earlier fixed-parameter SSMs (S4) could not do. Selectivity rules out the fast causal convolution used before, so decoding uses a hardware-aware parallel scan rather than a naive sequential recurrence. The block is a single residual path with no attention and no MLP: essentially Mamba block = gated conv1d shortcut + selective SSM, pre-norm residual. The state is a fixed-size (batch, d_inner, d_state) tensor per layer, CONSTANT in sequence length, so there is NO KV cache at all: per-token decode cost is O(d_model * d_state) state bytes instead of O(2 * L * d_h * d_k) KV bytes. That is the defining serving consequence and the reason long-context SSM decoding does not degrade with context length.
  speedup_reported: the retired record's text was materially fuller (538 chars vs 408) and is RETAINED here rather than discarded. Its text: 5x higher inference throughput than Transformers, against the paper's own GPT-3-style Transformer baselines at matched size; Mamba-3B matches Transformers twice its size in pretraining and downstream evaluation, and performance improves up to million-token sequences. The throughput figure is the authors' own reference implementation on A100 GPUs with their custom kernels and is not a tuned-engine number; published 5x claims for Mamba have consistently shrunk once engines run the model with generic PyTorch rather than the fused scan.
  AFFILIATIONS: left as-is on this record; the sweep verified it against the paper.
